svg.text: Глава 17 · IPv6 как развитие стека TCP/IP
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0514:c01–p0545:c01 · PDF 514–545 · printed 513–544
1 · Address architecture
128-bit hexadecimal addresses · prefix/CIDR structure · no classful A/B/C
One interface can hold several addresses with different roles/scopes
Global · link-local · ULA plus unspecified and loopback special forms
Unicast · anycast · multicast
Solicited-node multicast narrows local discovery traffic compared with broadcast-style ARP
2 · IPv6 packet processing
Fixed 40-byte base header → predictable mandatory parsing
Traffic Class · Flow Label · Payload Length · Next Header · Hop Limit
Extension headers carry optional routing/fragment/security/options information
Next Header forms a chain toward TCP/UDP/ICMPv6 or another extension
Transit routers do not fragment; endpoint adapts after Packet Too Big feedback in source model
3 · ICMPv6 and Neighbor Discovery
ICMPv6 → diagnostics/errors + transport for ND messages
RS → ask for routers · RA → prefix/MTU/default-router/autoconfig information
NS / NA → Duplicate Address Detection + link-layer address resolution
Solicited-node multicast avoids broad local broadcast for neighbor lookup
ND hop-limit validation keeps these messages local to the link in source model
Address resolution is therefore part of ND, not a separate ARP protocol
4 · Diagnostic dependency chain
Address exists → verify scope/source-selection compatibility
RA received → verify prefix/default-router/MTU, not just packet presence
DAD passed → address usable; ND resolves next-hop link-layer identity
ICMPv6 Packet Too Big → endpoint must adapt transmission size
Then validate routed reachability beyond the local link
Do not treat working IPv4 as evidence that IPv6 control plane is healthy
5 · Coexistence: dual stack and tunnels
Dual stack → independent IPv4 + IPv6 addresses/routes/DNS parameters
Application/name resolution chooses which family to use
Source describes Happy-Eyeballs-style preference testing
Tunnel → passenger packets remain unchanged inside transit protocol
GRE / 6to4 are source transition examples, not current recommendations
6 · Coexistence: translation
IPv6-only ↔ IPv4-only requires protocol/address translation in source model
DNS64 synthesizes an IPv6 representation for an IPv4 destination
Routing directs synthesized prefix toward NAT64
NAT64 keeps address+port mapping and translates packet headers both directions
Source example contains an inconsistent translator IPv4 literal; not silently corrected
Operational reading rule
IPv6 incident → addresses/scope → RA/default router → DAD/ND → next hop → ICMPv6/MTU → global route → transition mechanism.
Dual stack, tunnel and translation add different failure domains; identify the actual path before changing configuration.
No executable OS/router syntax is supplied by the chapter.
p0546:c01 starts Part-IV questions · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
